Therefore the two unconnected components are connected with a period, giving the target SMILES.

method.method_draft: First describe the drawn structure, ignoring all curved arrows. Encode the separate amine component as aniline: Nc1ccccc1. Then trace the imide reagent from one carbonyl around the fused norbornene/alkene skeleton to the second carbonyl and imide nitrogen, giving O=C1C2C3C=CC(C3)C2C(=O)N1. Continue from the imide nitrogen through the N-O-sulfonyl substituent as N1OS(=O)(=O)c1ccccc1, with the phenyl ring on sulfur. Join the two disconnected components with a period to obtain Nc1ccccc1.O=C1C2C3C=CC(C3)C2C(=O)N1OS(=O)(=O)c1ccccc1.

Use SMILES ring-closure syntax for the fused bicyclic imide and phenyl rings.
